paragraphs: R’ Yaakov son of R’ Elazar.

[Midrash Tehillim 19:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.19.2) cites him saying, “They knew that their God is truthful, and they do not flatter Him.” A parallel appears in [Yoma 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.69b.16) under R’ Elazar. Hyman reports that the glosses of רש״ב on Tehillim say it SHOULD READ R’ Yaakov bar Elazar. Hyman calls this mistaken: the glossator overlooked [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.7.3.9) and [the end of Megillah, chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.3.7.6), where, he says, the correct reading is R’ Yitzchak son of R’ Elazar. Hyman claims that Midrash Tehillim had the initials R-Y, which became R’ Yaakov, and that in Yoma the name R’ Yaakov was lost, leaving only R’ Elazar.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The linked Midrash names Yaakov son of Elazar. Yoma names Rabbi Elazar. The two linked Yerushalmi passages name Rabbi Yitzchak son of Elazar, with La’zar in Megillah.
The gloss Hyman attributes to Rashab has yet to be independently collated. The initials and proposed loss of a name are Hyman’s explanation.
Hyman favors Yitzchak in his discussion, yet the printed article (vol. II, pp. 777–778) ends by saying Yaakov was lost from Yoma.
